slides.title: Why churn is rising
Churn is rising almost only in SMB, which holds 80% of customers but just 24% of ARR

claims.claim: SMB churn jumped while mid-market and enterprise stayed below 1% a month
evidence: Monthly logo churn H1 2025 → H1 2026: SMB 0.02 → 0.031; Mid-market 0.006 → 0.008; Enterprise 0.002 → 0.002

claims.claim: SMB is most of the customer count but a small part of the revenue
evidence: SMB share of customers 0.797297; share of ARR 0.244186 (mid-2026)

claims.claim: Weighted by ARR, company churn is 1.2% a month in H1 2026 (0.8% in H1 2025), against 2.6% (1.7%) by customer count, using mid-2026 segment sizes
The board dashboard's "Monthly churn: 1.4% → 2.3%" does not define the measure and matches neither weighting

slides.title: Within SMB, the 2025 promotion cohort accounts for 56% of the customers who leave each month

claims.claim: 56.4% of SMB customers leaving each month came through the 2025 promotion
evidence: SMB monthly logo churn: Other SMB H1 2025 0.02; Other SMB H1 2026 0.021; All SMB H1 2026 0.031; Promotion cohort H1 2026 0.049095
Promotion-cohort churn derived: (5,900 × 3.1% − 3,800 × 2.1%) ÷ 2,100 = 4.9%, using mid-2026 customer counts

claims.claim: Promotion cohort: 36% of SMB customers, churning about 2.3 times as fast as other SMB customers
By ARR: about 38% of SMB revenue lost, because promotion accounts are about half the size of others
evidence: the ARR share assumes leavers are of average size within each group

claims.claim: Other SMB: churn barely moved, even after Inkwell launched in October 2025
evidence: Other SMB 2.0% H1 2025 vs 2.1% H1 2026

claims.claim: Most promotion-cohort customers who left did so within two months of the discount ending
evidence: briefing pack §6

slides.title: Price complaints come from promotion customers who never set the product up, not from the rest of SMB

claims.claim: Promotion leavers cite price nearly three times as often as other SMB leavers
evidence: Leavers citing price: Promotion cohort H1 2026 0.52; All SMB H1 2026 0.34; All SMB H1 2025 0.19; Other SMB H1 2026 0.18

claims.claim: Only 41% of promotion customers got started, against 72% of other cohorts
evidence: −31 pp
New customers sending five or more documents in month one: Promotion cohort 0.41; Other cohorts 0.72

claims.claim: Other SMB leavers cite price no more than in 2025; the promotion cohort needs onboarding before any price step
SMB customers who send fewer than five documents in month one churn at about three times the rate of those who send more
evidence: briefing pack §9

claims.claim: H1 2025 churners came almost entirely from outside the promotion, which started in February 2025

slides.title: Where prices can rise
Mid-market and enterprise can carry a rise because their existing customers keep expanding and stay for the product

claims.claim: Net revenue retention by segment, trailing 12 months to mid-2026
evidence: Enterprise 1.18; Mid-market 1.12; SMB 0.94; 2027 floor 1

claims.claim: Most of the revenue
evidence: $65.0M of the $86.0M ARR

claims.claim: Loyal to the product
evidence: They stay for integrations and audit trail

claims.claim: No Inkwell in large deals
evidence: Not seen in deals above 200 seats

claims.claim: Lead the 2027 rise with mid-market and enterprise renewals

slides.title: Mid-market can take 10%: conversion held in a 2024 test, and the rise pays unless renewals lose over 9% of ARR

claims.claim: A 10% higher list price left new mid-market conversion statistically unchanged
evidence: Conversion of new mid-market sign-ups, three-month test, 2024: Control price 0.236; 10% higher price 0.231

claims.claim: The rise pays until churn nearly doubles, to 1.6% a month from 0.8%
evidence: 10% price step, as tested
9.1% of repriced ARR can go before it stops paying

slides.title: SMB is the riskiest segment to reprice: Inkwell's $9 plan has cut Palisade's win rate by 13 percentage points

claims.claim: Inkwell's Starter plan costs 40% less than Palisade's SMB plan
evidence: List price $ per user per month, 2026: Palisade Business 29; Inkwell Pro 24; Palisade SMB 15; Inkwell Starter 9

claims.claim: Palisade now wins fewer than four in ten SMB deals where Inkwell is considered
evidence: −13 pp
SMB win rate where Inkwell was considered: H1 2025 0.51; H1 2026 0.38

claims.claim: Existing customers outside the promotion have not followed: churn 2.1% against 2.0% a year earlier
Inkwell launched Starter in October 2025; win rates are for new SMB deals, so they measure acquisition, not retention

slides.title: Which plan to choose
The CFO's plan would add about $7.6M of ARR in 2027, not $10.3M, once non-renewing contracts and caps are removed

claims.claim: ARR added by a 12% rise at renewal falls from $10.3M to $7.6M
evidence: 12% on all ARR 10.32; Mid-market not renewing −0.738; Enterprise not renewing −1.728; Enterprise 7% cap −0.288; 12% at 2027 renewals 7.566
$65.5M ARR renewing in 2027 × 12% CFO's price step − $0.3M (60% of enterprise renewals capped at 7%) = $7.6M ARR added, before churn
The CFO's $10.3M equals 12% of all $86.0M ARR; price changes apply only at renewal (briefing pack §3)

claims.claim: 33.3% of the $7.6M would come from SMB, the segment where churn is rising
Not renewing: $20.6M of ARR, mostly multi-year enterprise contracts, cannot be repriced in 2027
Caps: 60% of enterprise ARR cannot rise more than 7% a year
Promotion cohort: $0.5M of the SMB part would come from customers already leaving at 4.9% a month

slides.title: Every recommended price step rests on a 2024 test, the 2023 rise or a contract cap

claims.claim: Mid-market, +10%: Raise from January
evidence: Repriced ARR $34.9M; ARR added $3.5M; Break-even loss 9.1%
2024 test on new sign-ups: conversion 23.1% against 23.6%, not significant

claims.claim: Enterprise, +7%: Raise at renewal
evidence: Repriced ARR $9.6M; ARR added $0.7M; Break-even loss 6.5%
Cap on 60% of enterprise ARR; churn flat at 0.2% a month

claims.claim: Other SMB, +8%: Raise with a control group
evidence: Repriced ARR $16.6M; ARR added $1.3M; Break-even loss 7.4%
2023: the same step cost about 3.6% of customers, before Inkwell existed

claims.claim: Promotion cohort, +12% (CFO): Hold in 2027
evidence: Repriced ARR $4.4M; ARR added $0.5M; Break-even loss 10.7%
Already loses about 45% of its customers a year; 52% of leavers cite price

claims.claim: Break-even loss = price step ÷ (1 + price step); the 2023 reaction was 0.5 percentage points more churn for six months, then 0.1, about 3.6% of customers in a year

slides.title: The segmented rise gives up only the part of the CFO's uplift that no test or precedent supports

claims.claim: Hold all prices in 2027: Gives up the rise where churn is low
evidence: ARR added $0M; Evidence: No step

claims.claim: CFO: 12% on every plan: Most ARR, but a third of it from SMB and some from the promotion cohort
evidence: ARR added $7.6M

claims.claim: Mid-market and enterprise only: Safest, but leaves untouched other SMB customers, whose churn is flat
evidence: ARR added $4.2M

claims.claim: Segmented, SMB with a control group: Recommended: tested steps, and a stop rule where the risk is highest
evidence: ARR added $5.5M

claims.claim: What separates the CFO plan from the recommendation
evidence: $5.5M recommended plan: mid-market 10%, enterprise 7%, other SMB 8% + $2.1M steps beyond any test, precedent or cap, incl. 12% on the promotion cohort = $7.6M CFO plan at 2027 renewals, before churn

claims.claim: Approve the segmented plan in December; revisit the other steps for 2028

slides.title: The plan reaches the 2027 growth target only if existing customers keep today's net revenue retention of 109%

claims.claim: ARR bridge to the 2027 target
evidence: ARR mid-2026 86; Existing customers at trailing NRR 7.98003; Mid-market and enterprise rise 4.157; Other SMB rise, net of 2023-like churn 0.682592; New customers needed 0.080382; 2027 target 98.9
$98.9M 2027 target − $86M ARR today − $7.98M trailing NRR − $4.2M MM and Ent rise − $0.7M other SMB, net = $0.1M new customers

claims.claim: Retention, not price, decides the target
evidence: ARR per percentage point of NRR $0.9M: 1% × $86.0M
New customers needed if mid-market reacts like SMB in 2023 $1.5M: $0.1M + 3.6% × $38.3M repriced ARR

claims.claim: The plan lifts NRR to about 115%, above the 100% floor

slides.title: How to run the plan
Four moves make up the 2027 plan, each at a price step with evidence behind it

claims.claim: Mid-market: raise 10% at renewal from January, the step tested on new sign-ups in 2024
evidence: $3.5M ARR added at renewals, before churn

claims.claim: Enterprise: raise 7% at renewal, the most that capped contracts allow, and apply it to all renewals
evidence: $0.7M ARR added at renewals, before churn

claims.claim: Other SMB customers: raise 8% at renewal, the 2023 step, keeping a control group at today's price
evidence: $1.3M ARR added before churn; about half survives a 2023-like reaction

claims.claim: Promotion cohort: no rise in 2027, and an onboarding push to get every account sending documents
evidence: $4.4M ARR in the cohort, held at today's price

claims.claim: List prices for new SMB customers are outside this plan; with Inkwell at $9, review them separately before any change

slides.title: Onboarding the promotion cohort could keep up to $1.0M of ARR a year, but it cannot halve SMB churn

claims.claim: ARR kept by onboarding the promotion cohort, first 12 months, upper bound
evidence: $4.4M ARR in the promotion cohort today, at full price × 22.9 pp more of it kept after 12 months at other SMB churn: 77.5% compared with 54.7% = $1.01M ARR kept in a year, at most, before programme cost

claims.claim: The ceiling assumes full activation; the evidence supports less
evidence: Ceiling: the cohort's churn falls from 4.9% a month to the 2.1% of other SMB customers from January
Activation explains only part of the gap: low users churn about three times as fast, so 41% activation predicts 2.9%, not 4.9%
If the rest is a lasting reaction to the discount ending, full activation cuts churn to 3.3% and keeps about $0.5M

claims.claim: Halving SMB churn, as proposed, means 1.55% a month, below the 2.1% of SMB customers the promotion never touched

slides.title: A March read-out and two stop rules let Palisade reverse course before churn costs more than the rise earns

claims.claim: 2027 pricing roadmap, December 2026 to end of 2027
evidence: Dec 2026 Plan approved; Q1 2027 March read-out; Mid-year review
Mid-market and enterprise: Renewals at +10% and +7%
Other SMB: +8%, control group; Continue only if the read-out clears
Promotion cohort: Onboarding push, no rise; Set 2028 price for active accounts
Leadership reporting: Churn by segment and cohort

claims.claim: Stop rules: pause SMB if repriced churn runs 0.5 percentage points above the control group, the 2023 peak; pause mid-market above 1.6% a month
Churn reporting by logo and by ARR replaces the undefined dashboard figure; the 2023 SMB reaction showed within six months and promotion exits within two

assumptions_and_uncertainties: Synthetic benchmark data; every figure from the briefing pack
Churn weightings use mid-2026 segment sizes; the board dashboard's "Monthly churn: 1.4% → 2.3%" does not define the measure and matches neither weighting
Promotion-cohort churn is derived using mid-2026 customer counts; the ARR share assumes leavers are of average size within each group
Trailing NRR may include past enterprise escalators; the SMB window includes promotion customers stepping up from 50% off to full price
The 2024 test covered new sign-ups, not renewals; how existing customers react at renewal is untested
Break-even spreads the loss evenly over 12 months and treats logo churn as ARR churn; Inkwell can still reach mid-market deals under 200 seats
Win rates are for new SMB deals, so they measure acquisition, not retention
The 2023 SMB step precedent was before Inkwell existed
The 15% target is reached only if existing customers keep today's 109% retention; retention, not price, decides the target
New-customer bookings are not in the briefing pack; if trailing NRR includes enterprise escalators, part of the enterprise rise is counted twice
If mid-market reacts like SMB in 2023, $1.5M of new customers would be needed
Onboarding ceiling assumes full activation; the evidence supports less; the briefing pack gives no programme cost; logo churn is applied to the cohort's ARR
List prices for new SMB customers are outside this plan; with Inkwell at $9, review them separately before any change

normalized.extraction_notes: The deck came as plain text with no images, so there was nothing to transcribe from pictures. Chart values are copied as raw decimals (shares) or $M. Waterfall 'base' series are left out, and reductions are shown with a minus sign. The Harvey-ball ratings (Evidence, Churn safety, Growth target) in the slide 14 table did not survive the text extraction; only the 'Weak'/'Strong' legend text remains. Section-divider slides (3, 7, 11, 16) have empty claims lists, though each repeats its executive-summary point. The slide 20 next-steps table is listed under next_steps.
